key_insight: Adding rule-derived labels did not consistently improve prediction over using all budgeted reported labels, and equal weighting worsened Brier scores across all summarized settings.
clinical_relevance: Expanding antibiotic-resistance training data with rule-derived labels may underestimate non-susceptibility risk rather than improve predictions.
method: Studied E. coli urine cultures at Stanford and UT Southwestern using reported-label budgets of 10%, 25%, 50% and 100%.
Compared logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting with reported labels alone versus several rule-label augmentation strategies.
Evaluated five patient-disjoint outer splits using Brier scores and paired patient-cluster bootstrap intervals.
evidence_signal: Tuning-selected augmentation had worse median Brier scores than the all-budget reported-only baseline in 38 of 40 drug–model–budget summaries.
watch_item: All rule-derived labels were susceptible, and UT Southwestern's rules were not locally validated, limiting confidence in transportability.
paper_title: Do Rule-Derived Labels Improve Prediction When Reported Labels Are Limited? A Two-Site Machine Learning Study
